findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

The three verify.md files share the same "Final local verification for PR 6025" header. That header doesn't claim more than it can back up: the test-suite and acceptance limits are marked ⚠️, CI at the final head is required before merge, and PR readiness and desktop GUI execution are explicitly not claimed. The historical numbers add up (11,534 + 198 + 153 = 11,885 tests passed; 14 + 1 = 15 skipped). I found no path where the documents report a user-facing claim as satisfied when it is false. The warnings below are about traceability and consistency only.

No fresh local unit-test run covers the final integrated head. The 140-test run was at audit commit 3e2f66f6d. R1 (81dfa82e9) ran only its 100 affected tests. The merge with main and the later YAML comment edit were not unit-tested locally. The Test Suite line discloses this, and CI is stated as a merge blocker. Make sure the merge decision depends on CI at the final SHA, not on this document.

Key evidence is cited but not included in this packet, so it can't be verified here: delivery-evidence/walkthrough.json, comment-review.json, phase-stamp-skips.log, audit-tests.log.gz, and review receipts 7cbda067…, f0d46677…, 0a988f06…, 1d96e4ff… and bac2388a…. The checklist marks Surface Evidence and Audit ✅ based on these artifacts. Those checkmarks hold only if the artifacts exist and match what the document says.

The 117CBF historical section says no completion stamp was bypassed and the ticket stayed in implement/in_progress. The new shared header says a 'supported skip' now records the branch-wide stamp limitation. That's consistent if the skip is a sanctioned workflow path, but a reader of the historical section could take the stamp as never skipped. Add a short cross-reference in the historical text pointing to the skip log.

The same N7QY4E-centric final header is copied word for word into the 4RGYMY and 117CBF tickets. Those tickets' own scope (test-only BDD repairs) gets ✅ for Build, Experience and Reconcile based on production-fix wording ('generator, dispatcher and status reuse the semantic helper'). Those claims don't describe M1 or M2. Per-ticket deltas would make the traceability more accurate.

Typecheck moved from ⚠️ in the 4RGYMY historical section to ✅ in the shared header, with the same strict step-file diagnostics now called 'documented pre-existing debt'. The facts haven't changed, but the status marker is more optimistic than before.
